name: Tseghakronism
summary: Tseghakronism (tseghakron, 'nation-religion') is the ethnic-nationalist doctrine of the Armenian commander Garegin Nzhdeh. It treats the race or root as a sacred community whose blood is to be kept undiluted, puts the nation's and state's interests above the individual's, sees the Turk as the nation's enemy, and calls for a spiritual renewal that joins modern science with the viable values of the past. The Republican Party of Armenia has named it as its ideological basis.
scope: Nzhdeh's own doctrine of the 1930s-40s as set out in his writings (court-filed extracts of 'The Struggle of Sons against Fathers' and an exposition of 'Tribal Religion Movement') and its self-described later adherents (Prime Minister Margaryan's 2003 statement for the Republican Party of Armenia), as RFE/RL and the CACI Analyst identify it. It does not take in the general Armenian nationalism of the Dashnak mainstream or the later governing record of the Republican Party, which was one party among others in government. Only positions the doctrine's texts state are answered; economic, institutional and most social questions are null.

notes: Fails or sits at the edge of the uncertainty rule by design: the doctrine's available texts cover only nation, race, homeland, culture and the enemy. Themes searched: economy, government and institutions, religion and church, liberty, ecology, technology, world and means, in the local corpus (nothing on the subject), RFE/RL, CACI Analyst, the Hetq interview, Sargsyan's full article and the ICJ Annex 3 extracts, plus web searches for English translations of Nzhdeh (the Danielyan 'Selected Works' is not openly available) and for scholarship on the doctrine (Armeniapedia was blocked by a bot check and the Armenian Weekly page returned nothing). Stated but not answered because the statements overreach the sources: territorial expansion (the extract says Armenia should expand 'justly', without a programme), vengeance on Turks and the cadre/youth idea (translation awkward, no institutional design), war as character-building. Nzhdeh's Nazi-era collaboration and the RPA's governing record are not counted as the doctrine's positions. Missing statements: none that two separate passages support without leaning on the compressed translations.
